# Lavendar Lewis

## Overview

- **Age:** Forty-five years old (v02:c21:p0044)  <sub>[v2 c21 P44](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0044)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c21 P40](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0040)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v2 c30 P30](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0030)</sub>
- **Origin:** Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v2 c21 P42](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0042)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Miss Lavendar  <sub>[v2 c21 P40](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0040)</sub>; Mother Lavendar  <sub>[v2 c27 P4](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0004)</sub>

## Appearance

Lavendar is a petite, pretty woman with an almost girlish face, pink cheeks, and dimples. She has thick, snow-white hair that is softly wavy and arranged in puffs and coils, accompanied by big, sweet, wood-brown eyes containing golden glints. She possesses a voice that sounds like white satin, tinkling water, and fairy bells, and she favors dainty dresses made of muslin, frills, and laces.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002), [v2 c23 P9](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0009), [v2 c27 P3](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0003)_

## Personality

Lavendar is a sweet, romantic, and imaginative soul who maintains a youthful heart and a lively sense of play. Though she can be sulky, proud, and stubborn when hurt, she is deeply affectionate, hospitable, and possesses a cheerful, bright disposition. She loves young people, beauty, and pretending, often resorting to dreams and imaginative play to combat loneliness. Despite her imaginative nature, she also exhibits a sensible and kindhearted approach to those around her.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P47](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0047), [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054), [v2 c21 P87](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0087), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019), [v2 c23 P28](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0028)_

- To maintain a cheerful, youthful spirit and escape loneliness  <sub>[v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c23 P9](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0009)</sub>
- To be reunited in love with Stephen Irving  <sub>[v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019), [v2 c28 P71](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0071)</sub>

## History

Lavendar Lewis lived a quiet, secluded existence in the secluded stone house known as Echo Lodge in Grafton. In her youth, she was engaged to Stephen Irving, but a silly quarrel, compounded by her own sulkiness and their mutual pride, led to a broken engagement, after which Stephen left for the United States. Following her mother's death, Lavendar remained at Echo Lodge, employing a series of young girls whom she sequentially designated 'Charlotta' for convenience. To stave off loneliness, she frequently engaged in imaginative play, setting tea for imaginary guests and inventing a little 'dream-boy' companion. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally stumbled upon Echo Lodge and became fast friends with Lavendar. Later, Anne introduced Stephen Irving's son, Paul, to Lavendar, which eventually led to Stephen Irving returning to Four Winds to seek her out. Stephen and Lavendar reconciled, overcoming their quarter-century separation, and were married in the garden of Echo Lodge under the honeysuckle arbor. After their wedding, they departed on a trip to the Pacific coast before moving to Boston, keeping Echo Lodge as a summer residence.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c23 P15](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0015), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019), [v2 c23 P23](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0023), [v2 c23 P26](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0026), [v2 c28 P59](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0059), [v2 c28 P70](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0070), [v2 c30 P10](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0010)_

## Background by volume

- Named Lavendar by her father because her mother's sheets were scented with lavender when they first met  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Her mother died when Lavendar was thirty-five years old  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Brok off her engagement to Stephen Irving twenty-five years prior due to a foolish quarrel and mutual pride  <sub>[v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009), [v2 c23 P15](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0015), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>
- Lived a secluded life at Echo Lodge with a succession of young hired girls named Charlotta  <sub>[v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Quotes

> A person must have some compensations. I don't believe I could live at times if I didn't pretend things.  <sub>[v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054)</sub>

> A broken heart in real life isn't half as dreadful as it is in books. It's a good deal like a bad tooth... It takes spells of aching and gives you a sleepless night now and then, but between times it lets you enjoy life and dreams and echoes and peanut candy as if there were nothing the matter with it.  <sub>[v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>

> Some are born old maids, some achieve old maidenhood, and some have old maidenhood thrust upon them.  <sub>[v2 c23 P13](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0013)</sub>

> What is the use of being an independent old maid if you can't be silly when you want to, and when it doesn't hurt anybody?  <sub>[v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054)</sub>
